metadata.title: PIRLS 2001 User Guide for the International Database: Supplement 1

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a PIRLS 2001 International Database user guide supplement describing the international versions of background questionnaires (student, teacher, school, and Learning to Read home survey) and the mapping from questionnaire items to international background variable names. It does not provide an analytic sample, scaling, or any model-based estimation procedure, so survey weights and replicate-weight methods are not specified here. For secondary analyses using PIRLS microdata, analysts should consult the main PIRLS 2001 user guide documentation for the complex survey design and the recommended weight variables in the international database. Because this supplement is questionnaire documentation rather than an empirical study, it does not report how weights would be applied to outcomes.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This supplement does not analyze student achievement outcomes or generate/transform cognitive scores; it only documents questionnaire items and their corresponding international background variable names. As a result, plausible values (PV-based achievement scores) are not part of the described workflow, and missing-data handling for PVs is not applicable in this document. The absence of missing-data handling details reflects that the supplement is a data documentation artifact rather than an empirical modeling paper.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined in this supplement. It provides international questionnaire item-to-variable mappings for PIRLS 2001 background questionnaires (student, teacher, school, and Learning to Read home survey) and does not restrict or filter any dataset for analysis.

data.outcome_summary: This document is not an empirical study; it is a PIRLS 2001 International Database user guide supplement that provides the international versions of background questionnaires. It explains how countries could adapt questionnaire wording using <NRC NOTE:> and <International Option> conventions, and it lists the international background variables corresponding to administered questionnaire items. The supplement presents variable names and labels for multiple questionnaire sections: student background, teacher background, school questionnaire, and the Learning to Read home survey, including the Reading Literacy student background questionnaire. It also provides a standardized item field-location convention (e.g., SG1-***, SH1-***, TG1-***, CG1-***), enabling secondary analysts to link questionnaire items to international variable codes. No achievement outcomes, benchmarks, or predictive modeling results are reported in this supplement.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided text is a questionnaire documentation supplement rather than a research article with an analytic dataset, sample sizes, or model results. There are no dependent variables, performance metrics, or ML methods evaluated; therefore, fields related to PV handling, missing-data handling for estimation, and main findings are not applicable in the sense of empirical results. The supplement’s purpose is to support secondary analyses by clarifying variable naming and questionnaire structure, not to estimate effects.
